distinguishing_features: Passive surface-energy modification (SLIPS liquid-infused porous layer) rather than an active temperature-cycling duty schedule
Interposes a low-modulus liquid film to lower adhesion energy and shift failure to shear-detachment, rather than inducing tensile thermal stress via CTE mismatch
Uses the process stream itself to derive the infused lubricant, changing interfacial physics rather than setpoint trajectories
Eliminates scheduled shutdowns through passive self-cleaning at operating shear rather than periodic thermal shock cycles
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce asphaltene adhesion to preheat-train surfaces so that deposit detaches under normal operating flow shear without requiring periodic active intervention (thermal cycling, shutdowns, or chemical/mechanical cleaning).
parsed.viable_reason: The SLIPS liquid film is assumed to survive hot crude at 2 m/s and remain a stable 50 µm low-modulus layer, but the stab ly, low-interfacial-tension asphaltene-compatible liquid would be drained/sheared off and dissolve into the crude stream, so the assumed τ_int ≈ 1 Pa and self-cleaning at 8.5 Pa is not physically credible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a liquid-infused porous (SLIPS) interfacial layer to trade adhesion-accumulation for shear-detachment in refinery preheat service is not a routine parameter tweak of the thermal-cycling prior art and would not be an obvious step to a skilled engineer.
